data.gender_notes: Davinder is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Davinder is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Dha’ meaning ‘God’ and ‘Vinder’ meaning ‘light’. This name represents the light that God bestows upon us. The name Davinder carries the meaning “God's light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Davinder usually hope their child will grow to embody god's light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Davinder belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's light.”

data.cultural_impact: The name Davinder is a beautiful blend of Hindu and Sikh influences. In Hinduism, the name reflects the divine embodiment of God as light, which is a reoccurring theme in Hindu mythology. In Sikhism, the name can also be interpreted as the divine light that illuminates the path of the individual towards the realization of their true self and achieving a union with the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Davinder roots in the belief that God is the eternal light that pervades and sustains all existence. It reminds us that just as the sun illuminates the earth, God illuminates our inner selves and guides us on our spiritual journey towards enlightenment and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Davinder means 'beloved of God'. It symbolizes a deep connection with the divine, and the belief that God is always with us, guiding and protecting us. The name inspires devotion, faith, and a strong spiritual foundation.

historical_references.reference: Davinder was a prominent Sikh military leader during the time of Maharaj Ranjit Singh, who ruled the Sikh Empire from 1799 to 1839. He is known for his military prowess and was a trusted general of Maharaj Ranjit Singh.

Davinder Singh Brar was a prominent Indian-American entrepreneur and philanthropist. He played a significant role in the Silicon Valley tech industry, co-founding several successful companies such as Silicon Graphics and Redback Networks.
